taxonomy.label: billing_dispute
taxonomy.definition: The customer believes a charge is WRONG: a duplicate charge, an amount that does not match their plan, extra seats they do not have, or a charge they do not recognize.

taxonomy.label: refund_request
taxonomy.definition: The customer accepts the charge was valid when made but asks for money back: unused time after a downgrade, an accidental renewal, changing their mind.

taxonomy.label: technical_outage
taxonomy.definition: The service is broken or unavailable, typically for many users or the whole organization at once: errors, downtime, sync or webhook failures, crashes.

taxonomy.label: account_access
taxonomy.definition: A specific user or organization cannot sign in or verify identity while the service itself is up: passwords, 2FA, lockouts, SSO configuration.

taxonomy.label: feature_request
taxonomy.definition: The customer asks for a new capability or a change in behaviour. Nothing is broken.

taxonomy.label: churn_risk
taxonomy.definition: The customer states an intent to cancel, leave, not renew, or switch to a competitor.

rules: churn_risk takes precedence over every other label whenever the customer states an intent to cancel, leave, not renew or switch, even if they also report a bug or ask for a refund.
A charge the customer did not expect or does not recognize is billing_dispute, not refund_request.
If sign-in fails because the whole service is down, use technical_outage; if only one user or organization is affected while the service is up, use account_access.

few_shot_pool.label: refund_request

few_shot_pool.label: technical_outage
few_shot_pool.email: Webhooks have stopped firing for every one of our projects since 14:00 UTC, and your API is returning 500 errors.

few_shot_pool.label: churn_risk
few_shot_pool.email: Honestly the price jump is too much for us. Unless something changes we'll cancel at renewal next month.

few_shot_pool.label: churn_risk
few_shot_pool.email: Your competitor includes SSO for free. We're evaluating a switch, so give me a reason to stay.

few_shot_pool.label: billing_dispute
few_shot_pool.email: Our annual invoice applied last year's list price instead of the 15% discount written into our contract.

few_shot_pool.label: refund_request
few_shot_pool.email: We bought the onboarding package but our project was cancelled before kickoff. Can that fee be returned?

few_shot_pool.label: technical_outage
few_shot_pool.email: Search returns no results for anyone in our workspace since last night, even for documents we opened today.

few_shot_pool.label: account_access
few_shot_pool.email: My authenticator app was on my old phone, which I lost. How do I get back into my account?

few_shot_pool.label: feature_request
few_shot_pool.email: Please let us set different approval limits per department instead of one global limit.

few_shot_pool.label: churn_risk
few_shot_pool.email: Leadership has asked us to consolidate tools. We will not be renewing unless you can match our new vendor.

test_set.label: billing_dispute
test_set.email: I was charged $49 twice this month for the same Pro subscription. Please fix this.
test_set.rationale: Duplicate charge the customer believes is wrong -> billing_dispute.

test_set.label: refund_request
test_set.email: I downgraded to Basic last week but still have 20 days of Pro left. Can I get the difference back?
test_set.rationale: Valid charge, asks for money back for unused time after a downgrade -> refund_request.

test_set.label: billing_dispute
test_set.email: There's a $12.99 charge called 'NX*ADDON' on my statement. I never signed up for any add-on.
test_set.rationale: Unrecognized charge -> rule 2 says billing_dispute, not refund_request.

test_set.label: technical_outage
test_set.email: Since about 9am none of my team can load dashboards - we all get error 503.
test_set.rationale: Whole team sees 503 errors -> service broken -> technical_outage.

test_set.label: account_access
test_set.email: I reset my password but the 2FA code never arrives on my new phone, so I'm locked out.
test_set.rationale: Single user cannot verify identity while service is up -> account_access.

test_set.label: feature_request
test_set.email: Can you add dark mode to the mobile app? My eyes would thank you.
test_set.rationale: Asks for a new capability, nothing broken -> feature_request.

test_set.label: churn_risk
test_set.email: Third outage this month. If sync breaks again I'm moving our 40 seats to Competitor X.
test_set.rationale: Reports an outage but states intent to switch -> rule 1 precedence -> churn_risk.

test_set.label: technical_outage
test_set.email: I can't log in - and your status page says the whole login service is down?
test_set.rationale: Login fails because the whole service is down -> rule 3 -> technical_outage.

test_set.label: feature_request
test_set.email: Would be great if exports supported CSV with custom delimiters for our ERP import.

test_set.label: churn_risk
test_set.email: Please cancel my plan at the end of this cycle; we found a cheaper tool. Also refund the last month?
test_set.rationale: Intent to cancel plus a refund ask -> rule 1 precedence -> churn_risk.

test_set.label: billing_dispute
test_set.email: You billed us for 25 seats but we only have 18 active users.
test_set.rationale: Charged for seats they do not have -> amount is wrong -> billing_dispute.

test_set.label: account_access
test_set.email: Our SSO login stopped accepting our Okta assertions after your update yesterday - only our org seems affected.
test_set.rationale: Only one organization affected while the service is up -> rule 3 -> account_access.

reasoning_examples.question: A plan costs $20 per seat per month. A team of 5 pays monthly. What do they pay per year in dollars?
A job processes 90 documents per hour. How many hours are needed for 400 documents, rounded up to whole hours?

reasoning_test.question: A team plan costs $15 per seat per month. The team has 12 seats and pays annually with a 20% discount. What is the annual cost in dollars?
reasoning_test.worked: Monthly list = 15 x 12 = 180. Annual list = 180 x 12 = 2160. Discount 20% -> 2160 x 0.8 = 1728.

reasoning_test.question: A support queue receives 240 tickets per day. An AI assistant auto-resolves 35% of them; each agent resolves 16 of the remaining tickets per day. How many agents are needed?
reasoning_test.worked: Remaining = 240 x 0.65 = 156. Agents = 156 / 16 = 9.75 -> must round up to 10 whole agents.

reasoning_test.question: Input costs $4 per million tokens and output $20 per million. A request uses 3,000 input and 500 output tokens. What do 10,000 such requests cost in dollars?

A cache write costs 1.25x the base input price and a cache read 0.1x. A 10,000-token prefix is used by 5 requests within the cache lifetime. How many base-price token equivalents are billed for the prefix in total?
reasoning_test.worked: Request 1 writes: 10,000 x 1.25 = 12,500. Requests 2-5 read: 4 x 10,000 x 0.1 = 4,000. Total = 16,500.

reasoning_test.question: An SLA requires 99.5% availability over a 30-day month. How many minutes of downtime are allowed?
reasoning_test.worked: Minutes in month = 30 x 24 x 60 = 43,200. Allowed downtime = 43,200 x 0.005 = 216.
